claims.claim: Copilot only surfaces organisational data to which the individual user has at least view permissions
claims.locator: How does Microsoft Copilot use your proprietary organizational data?: 'Microsoft Copilot only surfaces organizational data to which individual users have at least view permissions.'

claims.claim: Every Copilot prompt runs in the security context of the user who started it
claims.locator: Supported conditions and actions, Note: 'All Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts run in the security context of the user who initiates the prompt.'

claims.claim: Everyone except external users is a built-in SharePoint group that automatically includes all internal users
claims.locator: What is the 'Everyone except external users' (EEEU) report?: 'EEEU is a built-in SharePoint group that automatically includes all internal users but excludes any external guests.'

claims.claim: Governance reports look for sites with thousands of users, EEEU permissions and sharing links of the types Anyone, People in the organization and Specific people
claims.locator: What are snapshot reports? and What are activity reports?

claims.claim: ATLAS AML.T0085 is named Data from AI Services and describes adversaries using access to a victim organisation's AI-enabled services to collect proprietary or otherwise sensitive information
claims.locator: ATLAS.yaml technique AML.T0085, name and description

claims.claim: ATT&CK T1213.002 is Data from Information Repositories: Sharepoint
claims.locator: Technique page title and ID

claims.claim: Copilot interactions are logged with Operation CopilotInteraction and Workload Copilot, and the payload is in CopilotEventData
claims.locator: Common properties in Copilot audit logs: Operation, Workload rows; S2 schema EntityType CopilotInteractionAuditRecord property CopilotEventData

claims.claim: AccessedResources is defined as references to all resources (files, documents, emails, etc.) which Copilot accessed in response to the user's request, with sub-properties ID, SiteUrl, ListItemUniqueId, Type, Name, SensitivityLabelId, Action, PolicyDetails, Status
claims.locator: Common properties in Copilot audit logs, AccessedResources row

claims.claim: Action commonly has the values read, create, modify; Status says whether the action on a resource was a success or failure; PolicyDetails is used when access was blocked or restricted by a policy and can include PolicyId and PolicyName
claims.locator: AccessedResources row: Action, PolicyDetails and Status bullets

claims.claim: AppHost identifies the hosting application; BizChat is the Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat client; Word and Teams are values
claims.locator: AppHost row and Common AppHost scenarios table

claims.claim: ThreadId is the ID of the Copilot and user interaction thread; Messages carries message IDs with isPrompt; ClientRegion is the user's region when they performed the operation
claims.locator: Audit Copilot schema definitions table and schema XML (MessageData isPrompt)

claims.claim: Auditing captures the Copilot activity of search but not the actual user prompt or response; use eDiscovery or the AI interaction view in DSPM for AI; device identity is not included in audit details
claims.locator: Compliance management considerations for Microsoft 365 Copilot, bullets on auditing and device identity

claims.claim: Prompts and responses in activity explorer are displayed to members of the Microsoft Purview Content Explorer Content Viewer role group
claims.locator: View data from your policies, step 2

claims.claim: ClientIP can be the IP address of a trusted application calling the service on behalf of the user
claims.locator: Common schema, ClientIP row

claims.claim: Audit (Standard) retains records 180 days; Audit (Premium) default policy retains records whose Workload is AzureActiveDirectory, Exchange, OneDrive or SharePoint for one year; other records 180 days by default
claims.locator: Audit (Standard) 180-day audit log retention; Audit (Premium) Long-term retention of audit logs; Audit log retention policies

claims.claim: The numeric RecordType of a CopilotInteraction record is 261
claims.locator: Audit log examples of CopilotInteraction, Example 1: RecordType: 261

claims.claim: SensitivityLabelId is the ID of the sensitivity label assigned to the resource; example value f41ab342-8706-4188-bd11-ebb85995028c
claims.locator: AccessedResources row and its example

claims.claim: When a label applies encryption, users must have the EXTRACT usage right as well as VIEW for the AI app to return the data
claims.locator: Sensitivity labels and AI interactions, second bullet

claims.claim: With VIEW but not EXTRACT, Copilot will not summarise the content but can reference it with a link; EXTRACT is the right to copy text
claims.locator: Information protection considerations, first bullet; section Copilot honors existing protection with the EXTRACT usage right

claims.claim: A DLP policy for the Copilot location with the condition Content contains Sensitivity labels stops Copilot processing the item's content, but the item can still appear in citations
claims.locator: Block files and emails with sensitivity labels from being processed

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels applied to containers (groups and sites) are not inherited by items in those containers
claims.locator: Information protection considerations, bullet on container labels

claims.claim: CopilotActivity has columns TimeGenerated, ActorName, SrcIpAddr, AppHost, RecordType and the dynamic column LLMEventData (parsed LLM event data)
claims.locator: Columns table

claims.claim: OfficeActivity has columns Operation, UserId, ClientIP, UserAgent, Site_Url, SourceFileName, OfficeObjectId, SensitivityLabelId
claims.locator: Columns table

claims.claim: ATT&CK detection guidance for T1213.002 looks for privileged or rarely used accounts performing bulk access to SharePoint files within a short time window
claims.locator: Detection strategy DET0500, Detecting Abnormal SharePoint Data Mining by Privileged or Rare Users

claims.claim: JailbreakDetected is a flag on a prompt message and XPIADetected marks a detected cross prompt injection attack on an accessed resource
claims.locator: Messages row and AccessedResources row

claims.claim: ATLAS: AI agents may be configured to have access to tools and data sources that are not directly accessible by users; AML.T0085.000 is RAG Databases
claims.locator: ATLAS.yaml AML.T0085 description and AML.T0085.000 name

claims.claim: OWASP LLM08:2025 Vector and Embedding Weaknesses recommends permission-aware vector stores and detailed immutable logs of retrieval activities
claims.locator: Prevention and Mitigation Strategies: Permission and Access Control; Logging and Monitoring

claims.claim: OWASP LLM02:2025 Sensitive Information Disclosure: limit access to sensitive data based on the principle of least privilege
claims.locator: Prevention and Mitigation Strategies, Enforce Strict Access Controls

claims.claim: Security filter pattern: a group_ids field and the filter group_ids/any(g:search.in(g, 'group_id1, group_id2')); the principal is just a string with no authentication through it; the application must apply filters to every query
claims.locator: About the security filter pattern; Apply the security filter in the query

claims.claim: Native permission filtering: x-ms-query-source-authorization carries the delegated user's token, Authorization carries the caller's token; permission refresh does not provide immediate revocation
claims.locator: Pattern for native support for POSIX-like ACL and RBAC scope permissions; Permission freshness

claims.claim: ATLAS AML.T0012 is Valid Accounts; ATT&CK T1078.004 is Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts
claims.locator: ATLAS.yaml AML.T0012 name; ATT&CK page S16 title

claims.claim: FileAccessed: user or system account accesses a file on a SharePoint or OneDrive site; UserAgent is provided by the client or browser; ObjectId is the full path and equals SiteUrl plus SourceRelativeUrl plus SourceFileName; ListItemUniqueId identifies the list item; SharePointFileOperation is record type 6
claims.locator: SharePointAuditOperation enum FileAccessed; SharePoint Base schema; SharePoint file operations; AuditLogRecordType table

claims.claim: Restricted access control: users not in the specified group cannot access the site or its content even if they had prior permissions or a shared link; up to 10 groups per site; Copilot and organisation-wide search honour it; PowerShell Set-SPOTenant -EnableRestrictedAccessControl, Set-SPOSite -RestrictedAccessControl and -AddRestrictedAccessControlGroups
claims.locator: Introduction; Restrict access to all SharePoint sites; Manage site access restriction by using PowerShell

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery does not change permissions, applies to SharePoint sites and not OneDrive, is a temporary governance control, can take more than a week on sites with more than 500,000 items, is set with Set-SPOSite -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch
claims.locator: Note under introduction; Frequently asked questions; Use PowerShell

claims.claim: Restricted SharePoint Search: allow list of up to 100 SharePoint sites, not a security boundary, retiring with new enablement blocked starting July 31, 2026
claims.locator: Important notice at top; How to use Restricted SharePoint Search; How does Restricted SharePoint Search work?

claims.claim: Data access governance: the site permissions report is a snapshot highlighting sites with thousands of users or EEEU permissions; activity reports track the last 28 days of sharing link creation and sharing with everyone
claims.locator: What are snapshot reports?; What are activity reports?

claims.claim: CopilotInteraction record properties used in the room (AccessedResources Name, SiteUrl, listItemUniqueId, SensitivityLabelId, Action; UserId, CreationTime, ClientRegion, AppHost, ThreadId) and the absence of prompt and response text
claims.locator: Common properties in Copilot audit logs; S18 compliance considerations for the missing prompt text

claims.claim: A label without encryption does not restrict the assistant; site labels are not inherited by items; PolicyDetails and Status meaning
claims.locator: Information protection considerations (container labels; DLP bullet 'whether encrypted or not'); S1 AccessedResources row for PolicyDetails and Status

claims.claim: SharePoint FileAccessed records carry ClientIP, UserAgent and ListItemUniqueId
claims.locator: Common schema ClientIP; SharePoint Base schema UserAgent and ListItemUniqueId

claims.claim: Restricted access control changes access; Restricted Content Discovery changes discovery only and is temporary; the DLP policy for the Copilot location excludes labelled items from processing while they can still appear in citations
claims.locator: S19 introduction; S5 note and FAQ; S17 Block files and emails with sensitivity labels

claims.claim: In the security filter pattern the application adds a filter listing the caller's groups and must apply it to every query
claims.locator: About the security filter pattern

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels have a priority order defined by compliance admins, and a higher priority number usually denotes higher sensitivity
claims.locator: Sensitivity labels and AI interactions, AI app-specific information

quiz_map.support: Microsoft states that Copilot only surfaces organisational data to which the individual user has at least view permissions, and that every prompt runs in the security context of the user who started it.
Microsoft says auditing captures the Copilot activity of search, but not the actual user prompt or response.
The label is a marker only, and the item is read if permissions allow
Owners and their teams reading their own labelled content.
the application connects to the index with its own service identity, which can read everything, and returns whatever matches.
A stolen account sweeps many themes in a dense burst, often from a new region and outside the user's normal hours.
Users who already have access can still open the content directly.
Region, network and hours matched his normal pattern, and nothing suggested another person.
Microsoft states that Copilot only surfaces organisational data to which the individual user has at least view permissions.
The ID of the sensitivity label on the resource
The record holds no prompt text and no answer text.
ThreadId identifies the conversation, so records with the same ThreadId belong to one chat.
An entry with PolicyDetails and a failure status means the control stopped the read.
A real user reached content they should not see, through a permission gap.
The rule fired on a user who is an authorised owner of the content, such as a member of the group that owns the site.
The evidence says the account may not be in its owner's hands.
That last field is the unique identifier of the item, so it lets you connect a resource the assistant accessed to a file the same account later opened by hand.
The rule misfired, for example the entry shows the read was blocked.
The exposure ends only when the permission changes.
Work in this order, and do not skip the last step.
A retrieval with an empty filter is the clearest sign of a broken control.
